name: design-review
description: Four blind readings of a design document, side by side, each through its own lens (comprehension, design, readiness, codebase), then a refuter for what only one saw; the document is yours to change, so the findings come to you

steps.title: Comprehension reading
steps.prompt:
Read, without changing any file, the design document {doc} (inside this repository). What it is for: {goal}

You are one of four readers working apart, each through its own lens; yours is comprehension. Read as a person new to this project would. First paraphrase, in `summary`, in two short paragraphs: what the document proposes, and how the existing system works as the document tells it. Then report as a finding each section you could not paraphrase, each term specific to this project that nothing in the document defines, and each step that assumes setup the document does not state. General engineering terms are not findings. Report each in `findings` with `where` (`doc:line` or the section heading), `what`, `evidence_class`, `cause` and `proof` (the quoted passage). Say plainly when there is none.

steps.title: Design reading
steps.prompt:
Read, without changing any file, the design document {doc} (inside this repository). What it is for: {goal}

You are one of four readers working apart, each through its own lens; yours is the design: stress-test it. Look for assertions about behaviour, performance or constraints that carry no justification, failure modes the document does not address, scaling limits, security concerns it leaves out, and alternatives it does not weigh. Report each in `findings` with `where` (`doc:line` or the section heading), `what`, `evidence_class`, `cause` and `proof` (the passage, and the case that breaks it). Say plainly when there is none.

steps.title: Readiness reading
steps.prompt:
Read, without changing any file, the design document {doc} (inside this repository). What it is for: {goal}

You are one of four readers working apart, each through its own lens; yours is readiness: read it as the engineer who must implement it tomorrow. Report as findings every design decision the document leaves to the implementer (a schema, a signature, an error strategy, where a file goes), every file the work will touch that the document does not list, and every behaviour with no test named. Report each in `findings` with `where` (`doc:line` or the section heading), `what`, `evidence_class`, `cause` and `proof` (the passage, or the file the work would touch). Say plainly when there is none.

steps.title: Codebase reading
steps.prompt:
Read, without changing any file, the design document {doc} (inside this repository). What it is for: {goal}

You are one of four readers working apart, each through its own lens; yours is the codebase: check the document against the code. Report as findings the files, symbols, endpoints or tables the document says exist now and do not; descriptions of current behaviour the code contradicts (a blocker: every later reader inherits the false statement); and existing utilities the document proposes to rewrite. Files and symbols the document proposes to create are not findings. Report each in `findings` with `where` (`doc:line` or the section heading), `what`, `evidence_class`, `cause` and `proof` (the command or the code that shows it). Say plainly when there is none.

steps.title: Decide what only one saw
steps.prompt: Decide, without changing any file, the findings on the design document {doc}. What it is for: {goal}
